translator: Claude (AI), draft, not reviewed by a Hittitologist
intro: Manuscript A of Muršili II's so-called Fourth Plague Prayer, addressed to the assembly of the gods (CTH 378.4; Singer no. 13), joined from KUB 14.13 + KUB 23.124. After a roster of the gods of the Hittite cult centres, Muršili recalls how the gods once favoured Ḫatti, how under his grandfather enemies and plague emptied the land and its temples, how his father restored the cults, and how since his father's Egyptian campaign the plague has become permanent while oracles fail to reach the gods. He asks how he can restore their cults when household, land and army are dying. The tablet looks unfinished: it has blank lines, isolated PAB signs and about twenty uninscribed lines at the end.

paras.en: Gods, my lords: the Storm-god Multarriḫu ('the Proud'); the two Lords of Landa; Iyarri; the gods of Ḫatti; the gods of Arinna; the gods of Zippalanda; the gods of Tuwanuwa; the gods of Ḫupišna; the gods of Durmitta; the gods of Ankuwa; the gods of Šamuḫa; the Storm-god of Šarišša; the gods of Šarišša; the gods of Ḫurma; the gods of Ḫanḫana; the gods of Karaḫna; the gods of Ellaya; Kamrušepa of Taniwanda; the gods of Zarruwiša; the Storm-god of Liḫzina; the Tutelary Deity of the army camp of the father of My Majesty; Uliliyašši of Parmanna, who is in Maraššantiya; the gods of Kattila; the Storm-god of Ḫašuna; the gods (of?) Muwanu; the gods of Zazziša; the Telipinus; the temples of the god[s(?) …] that are ruined in the land; the gods of Šalpa; the Storm-god of Ar[…]!
Gods, my lords! Look, I, Muršili, your priest, have bowed down to you. Concerning the matter for which I have bowed down to you, hear me! [Lend me] (your) [ear], and hear me!

Gods, my lords! From of old you were turned in (favour) toward […], and you did [not] let mankind dry up(?). Mankind was numerous, and your servants, (the servants) of the gods, were many, and they set up thick bread and libation vessels for the gods, my lords. But you, gods, (my) lords, turned (your) back on mankind. It came about that in the time of my grandfather the land of Ḫatti was oppressed: […] perished through the enemy, and likewise perished through plague, and mankind became [few]; and your […], gods, […] became [f]ew. As for your temples, gods, my lords, which […]: the servants of one perished, and whoever (served) a god perished; the rites of the gods perished altogether, and no one performed them for you.

But when my father sat in kingship, you, gods, my lords, stood by him, and he resettled the empty land a second time. […] gods, my lords, in whichever temple [its] implements were lacking, and whichever god had perished — what my father was able (to do), he restored, but what he was not able (to do), he did not restore. Gods, my lords, you never became a burden to my father, and you never became a burden to me either; but now you are becoming a burden to me.

It came about that when my father went to the land of Egypt, from the day of Egypt the plague became permanent in the land […], and from th[at moment] the land of Ḫatti has been dying. My father kept consulting oracles, but he did not find you, gods, (my) lords, through oracles. I too kept consulting oracles about you, but I too did not find you, gods, my lords, through oracles.
[Only the sign PAB is written here, twice on each of two lines, followed by the single word ḫarran ('crushed'? 'ruined'?); its purpose is unclear.]
And to you […] as […] set up(?) […]
And since the gods […] but now [to you …] and to you […] after […] […] and he has no temple […] [Break.] [Only the sign PAB, on two lines.]
And (to) me […] And […] And to [you …] And to [you …] […]
If […] in(to) […] and to [you …] and […] [Break of about 32 lines.] […] land […] troops […] you […]
Gods, [my] lords! Since(?) […] if […] to the gods […]

…or else from the land, or from the troops and chariotry, I restored it for the gods, my lords. If I (am to) set the gods in order again — now, since household, land, troops and chariotry are dying on me, from what shall I set you, gods, in order again?
[Blank lines, with only the sign PAB written on two separate lines.]

Since he dies, [sign PAB twice], from what shall I set (you) in order again? Gods, take pity on me again from this (side?) [sign PAB], turn to me, and send the plague away from the land again! The cities in which there is dying — let it get better; and the cities in which (things are) we[ll] — let the plague not go back (there)! […] and I too (spoke?) again in (my) soul(?) as follows: '[…] (is) that matter of the god true? […] my father […] through oracles […], but I did not find it, and the land of Ḫatti … […] it […] through oracles […]' […] plea(?) […] [Traces of nine more lines.]
Gods, [my] lords […] there(?) […] determin[ed(?)] […] the land of [A]zz[i](?) … Ḫatti(?) […] … NAM … [The rest of the tablet, about twenty lines, was left uninscribed.]
